I don't just brush it off like a normal person. It just proves to me that I’m completely useless. It’s not just a mistake, it’s like this glaring proof that I'm a failure and I deserve whatever bad things happen to me, whatever financial ruin comes our way. I just can't stop feeling so incredibly guilty about all of it, just constantly replaying every little screw-up and thinking about how I'm dragging everyone down with me... turns.doctor_question: If the condo were no longer a problem tomorrow, do you think this heavy depressed feeling would go away?
turns.patient_response:
I mean... I really don't know. I have thought about that a lot, actually. Like, if we just put the place on the market and sold it, or if some magic wand waved and the mortgage was suddenly paid off, would I just wake up and be completely fine? 

But honestly, I don't think it would just vanish overnight. Because at this point, it feels like it has become more than just the stress about the money or the building itself. It has kind of settled deep into me. Most days, there is just this heavy, empty feeling right here in the center of my chest. It is almost like a physical weight, just sitting there from the moment I wake up until I finally fall asleep. 

And I go to work, and I am really just going through the motions. I am carrying these massive ceramic plates we use for the entrees, balancing them up my arm, walking back and forth from the hot line in the kitchen out to the dining room, and I am smiling at all my tables. I am doing the whole upbeat greeting routine, introducing myself, asking about their evening, laughing at their little jokes about the menu. But I am only smiling because I am supposed to, because my job and my tips literally depend on me looking happy and accommodating for the guests. I am not smiling because I actually feel anything good. Inside, I don't feel anything good at all. 

It is just that heavy emptiness, day after day. So even if the condo problem was completely resolved by tomorrow morning, I really think this feeling would still be there, just weighing me down while I am pouring water and clearing off tables. It is like it has become my normal state of being now, not just a reaction to the real estate, if that makes any sense.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient describes a persistent 'heavy, empty feeling' in their chest that lasts all day, every day, indicating a depressed and empty mood.

turns.doctor_question: Are you absolutely convinced that you deserve to be punished for what happened with the condo, even when other people tell you that isn’t true?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I mean... absolutely. I know I mentioned this earlier, but that's really the whole reason I'm sitting here talking to you right now. I just... I can't shake this feeling that I have completely and utterly let my family down. It's like this heavy weight sitting right on my chest, all the time. 

My wife, Sarah, she tries to tell me it's not my fault, that the market changed, that we made the decision together. She'll sit there on the couch with me after a shift and say, 'Honey, we're in this together, it's just a mortgage, we'll figure it out.' But I can't hear it. I just can't believe her, because I know I was the one pushing for it. I was the one looking at Zillow every night, talking about equity and investing in our future and all that stuff. I convinced her. And now we're stuck in this financial mess, and every time we have to look at the budget, I just feel this overwhelming guilt. 

And it's not just at home, either. Like I said before, it bleeds into my work at the restaurant. It's gotten so bad that even when I do something incredibly minor, like forgetting that side of garlic aioli for the fries, or ringing in a regular Coke instead of a Diet Coke—things that happen literally every single day in the service industry—my brain just immediately jumps to, 'See? You're completely useless.' It's like every dropped fork or forgotten ramekin is just further proof that I am fundamentally incompetent. 

And because I'm so useless, because I messed up so badly with the condo, I feel like I deserve all of this. I deserve the stress, I deserve the panic attacks about the bills, I deserve to feel this way. It's like it's my punishment for being so stupid and arrogant, thinking I could handle being a homeowner and providing for my family when I clearly can't even remember to ring in a side of sauce. So yeah, no matter what Sarah or anyone else says, I'm just completely convinced that I brought all of this on myself and I deserve whatever happens to me.
